title: Start with how it felt
summary:
This demonstration shows the structure of a future dream reflection. The program currently looks for a small set of familiar words in your account and displays a prepared text. It does not identify a hidden meaning or consult the research library to produce a personal interpretation.

Start with what you actually remember: where you were, what happened, and how you felt after waking. Choose one detail that caught your attention and write down your own association with it. If a familiar place brings a recent conversation or memory to mind, you can explore that connection as a personal hypothesis. There is no need to force a connection if none comes to mind.

Try separating events within the dream from the thoughts you had about them afterward. A scene can feel different depending on your own experience. Use the question below as a starting point. You decide whether this direction is useful; this example does not assess your health or establish facts about other people.
key_connection: Consider one remembered detail alongside the feeling you woke with. Any connection between them is yours to explore.
reflection_question: Which detail stays with you most, and what do you personally associate with it?
